title: Influence Of A 10-Week Complex Training Program On Improvements In Speed And Agility Among Female Basketball Players In Madiun
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of a 10-week physical training program on the speed and agility of female basketball athletes from Madiun City who are preparing for the East Java Provincial Sports Week. The study employed a quasi-experimental design because the researcher did not have full control over the subjects’ activities outside of training sessions. The study population consisted of 26 female basketball athletes who participated in player selection, while the sample comprised 13 athletes selected using purposive sampling based on the criterion of actively participating in training camps. The physical training program was conducted over 10 weeks at a frequency of twice per week, resulting in a total of 20 training sessions. Data analysis was performed using a paired-sample t-test to compare pre-test and post-test results for the speed and agility variables. title: The Effect of Using Boccia Equipment on the Accuracy of Throws by Athletes with Cerebral Palsy in the Sport of Boccia
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the use of BET (Boccia Equipment Tools) on the throwing accuracy of athletes with cerebral palsy in the sport of boccia. The research method used a quasi-experimental design with a pretest-posttest control group design approach. The study sample consisted of 34 athletes (17 in the experimental group and 17 in the control group). The research instrument used a validated boccia throwing accuracy test. Data analysis used normality tests, homogeneity tests, paired sample t-tests, independent sample t-tests, and the N-Gain Score test. title: The Effect of Aerobic Exercise Intervention on Reducing Blood Sugar Levels in an effort to prevent diabetes mellitus in students aged 7-12 years
abstract: This prevalence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in children has increased due to a sedentary lifestyle. This condition triggers an urgent need for preventive measures through measurable physical activity. This study aims to determine the effect of aerobic exercise intervention on reducing blood sugar levels as an effort to prevent T2DM in students aged 7–12 years. The research method used a quasi-experimental approach with a one-group pretest-posttest design. Subjects were selected through purposive sampling based on specific inclusion criteria. The intervention consisted of a structured moderate-intensity aerobic exercise program. Data on random blood glucose (RBG) levels were collected using a standard digital glucometer before and after the intervention. Data analysis was performed using the non-parametric Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test. The results showed a significant decrease in the mean random blood glucose levels of the subjects after the intervention. Consistent aerobic activity was proven to optimize insulin sensitivity and increase glucose uptake by muscle cells, thereby directly contributing to the stability of blood glucose regulation in children. title: The Relationship Between Concentration and Eye-Foot Coordination and Shooting Accuracy
abstract: In futsal, shooting accuracy is crucial, but many players still find it difficult to execute it well under pressure and in a variety of game scenarios during practice sessions and competitive matches. The purpose of this study was to investigate how Bintang Lima Futsal Club athletes' focus, eye-foot coordination, and shooting accuracy relate to one another. Purposive sampling was utilized to choose 24 male athletes between the ages of 16 and 18 for a quantitative correlational study. The Mitchell Soccer Test, the Grid Concentration Test, and a shooting accuracy test were among the tools used. Descriptive statistics, normality, linearity, and Pearson product-moment correlation tests were used to examine the data. Since all p-values were greater than 0.05, there was no significant correlation found between eye-foot coordination and shooting accuracy (r = 0.048; p = 0.825) or between concentration and shooting accuracy (r = 0.129; p = 0.584). These results show that eye-foot coordination and focus did not significantly influence shooting accuracy in this investigation. title: The Effect Of Circuit Training On Improving The Endurance Of Martial Arts Athletes In Tarung Derajat
abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine the effect of circuit training on improving the endurance of Tarung Derajat martial arts athletes in Bantul Regency. The study employed an experimental method using a one-group pretest-posttest design. The sample consisted of 12 athletes selected using total sampling. Endurance was measured using the Multistage Fitness Test (MFT) to determine VO₂Max values. The circuit training program was conducted over 6 weeks at a frequency of 3 times per week, totaling 16 sessions. Data analysis included tests of normality, homogeneity, and hypothesis testing using the Paired Sample t-Test. title: The Effect of Underhand Passing Drills on Volleyball Passing Skills Among Students at State Junior High School 1 Todanan
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of underhand passing drill training on volleyball underhand passing ability in extracurricular students of State Junior High School 1 Todanan. This study uses a quantitative approach with an experimental method using a one-group pretest-posttest design. The research sample consisted of 20 male students who were members of the volleyball extracurricular selected using a purposive sampling technique. The research instrument used the Brumbach Forearms Pass Wall Volley Test to measure students' underhand passing ability. The underhand passing drill training program was given for 12 meetings over a period of four weeks. Data analysis techniques included descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, the homogeneity test, and hypothesis testing using the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test. The results of this study indicate that underhand passing drill training has a significant effect on students' underhand passing ability in volleyball. title: The Effectiveness Of A Needs-Based Guidance Program In Reducing Academic Stress And Improving Performance On The Balance Beam
abstract: The study aims to build a guidance program based on guidance needs to reduce academic stress and improve performance on the balance beam, and to build an academic stress scale for third-year students of the College of Physical Education at the Universities of Dhi Qar and Al-Ain.The study aimed to identify the program's effectiveness in meeting guidance needs, reducing academic stress, and improving performance on the balance sheet for female students between pre- and post-tests in both groups، The research population consisted of (102) female students, divided int The pilot study sample consisted of (8) female students, the construction sample of (70) female students, and the application sample of (24) female students, divided into (12) students in the control group implementing the teacher's usual curriculum and (12) students in the experimental group implementing the guidance program. It was found that the psychological guidance program Based on guidance needs, it is able to reduce academic stress among students while performing skills, especially difficult ones. title: The Effectiveness of Cooperative Soccer Like Games on Gross and Social Motor
abstract: This study aims to test the effectiveness of soccer like games learning with a cooperative approach in improving gross motor skills and social skills of elementary school students. The research uses the design of Classroom Action Research (PTK) which is carried out in three cycles each of which includes the stages of planning, implementation of actions, observation, and reflection, with subjects of 45 elementary school students. The instruments used are the Test of Gross Motor Development (TGMD) tomeasure gross motor skills and the Social Skills Rating System (SSRS) to assess social skills, both of which are standardinstruments that are widely used in children's education and physical education research. The results showed an increase in gross motor score from 48.9 in cycle I to 66.6 in cycle II and 80 in cycle III, while social skills score increased from 33.3 in cycle I to 60 incycle II and 82.2 in cycle III. These findings show that game-based learning combined with a cooperative approach is effective in developing gross motor skills as well as social skills of elementary school students simultaneously.

title: Profile of Sports Injuries in Pencak Silat Athletes in the Lampung Contingent Competition Category at POMNAS XIX Central Java 2025
abstract: This study aims to identify and classify the types of sports injuries, as well as analyze the mechanism of injury in pencak silat athletes in the Lampung contingent competition category during the POMNAS XIX Central Java 2025 event. The method used is quantitative descriptive with purposive sampling technique, where the sample is focused on athletes who are identified as having an injury during competition. The initial population involved 17 athletes in the competition category, with analysis carried out on the total injury cases that occurred throughout the tournament. The results showed that there were 7 incidents of injuries covering four main types: muscle/superfacial bruises (57.2%), arthritis (14.3%), chondral injuries (14.3%), and lacerations (14.3%). The most common part of the body was injured was the head (42.85%), which was generally caused by impact during the slamming process. The majority of athletes needed a recovery time of 2 weeks (28.6%). title: The Relationship Between Goal Setting and Physical Fitness on Performance Badminton Athletes at SGS PLN Club
abstract: Athlete performance is influenced not only by physical factors but also by psychological aspect. However, research integrating goal setting and physiological fitness indicators such as resting heart rate (RHR) in badminton athletes is still limited. This study aims to analyze the relationship between goal setting and physical fitness measured through RHR among badminton athletes at SGS PLN Club, Bandung City. This study uses a quantitative approach with a correlational design. The sample consisted 30 athletes ages 13-18 years, selected using purposive sampling. Goal setting data were obtained through the Goal Setting Questionnaire (GSQ), while physical fitness was measured by average RHR over three consecutive days. Data analysis use pearson correlation with significant relationship between goal setting and RHR (r= -0.52; p= 0.003). the findings show that the higher the athlete’s ability to set goals, the better their cardiovascular fittnes level. Thus, goal setting is related fitness, which plays a role in badminton athlete performance

title: The Relationship Between Fear of Reinjury and Readiness to Return to Sport in Young Athletes Following Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Injury
abstract: The Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) injury is one of the most feared injuries by every athlete. This is because ACL injuries require a long healing process, starting from reconstruction to post-reconstruction rehabilitation. ACL injury patients often have a fear of re-injury when they perform a movement while returning to sports. This fear of re-injury can determine the patient's readiness to return to sports. This study examines the relationship between fear of reinjury and readiness to return to sports among young athletes. A descriptive correlational design was used in this study involving 20 young athletes. The ACL-RSI instrument, consisting of 12 questions and the TSK-11, consisting of 11 questions, were used in this study, where each subject was given a questionnaire containing fear of reinjury (TSK-11) and readiness to return to sports (ACL-RSI) once and then continued with data analysis using the Pearson correlation test with SPSS 27. The study indicates a significant relationship between fear of reinjury and readiness to return to sports among young athletes. title: Quality of Physical Education Lesson Planning at Elementary Schools Based on Teaching Practicum Students’ Perceptions
abstract: This study aimed to describe the quality of Physical Education (PE) lesson planning at elementry schools based on teaching practicum students’ perceptions. The study used an evaluative design with a descriptive quantitative approach. The subjects were 40 Physical Education students from FKIP Universitas Bengkulu who had completed their teaching practicum, selected using the Slovin formula from a population of 65 students with a 10% margin of error. Data were collected via a 4 point Likert scale questionnaire of 29 items across six dimensions: (1) formulation of learning objectives, (2) learning material planning, (3) learning strategies and models, (4) learning activities, (5) media and learning resources, and (6) assessment planning. All 29 items were valid (r=0.658-0.926 > r table=0.312) and the Cronbach Alpha coefficient was 0.984 (very reliable). Results showed overall PE lesson planning quality was Very Good (total score 3,904/4,640; 84.14%; mean=3.37). title: The Effect Of Supporter Pressure On Football Referees’ Decision-Making In Semarang U-18 Junior Premier League
abstract: This study aimed to examine the effect of supporter pressure on football referees’ decision-making accuracy in the Semarang U-18 Junior Premier League competition. A quantitative correlational design was employed. The participants consisted of 44 active referees from the Semarang City Football Association selected through total sampling. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire measuring supporter pressure and referee decision-making accuracy. Data were analyzed using validity, reliability, normality, linearity, and simple linear regression tests with IBM SPSS Statistics 25. title: The Effect of Small Sided Games Training Assisted by Blue Lock Anime on the Shooting Ability of SSB Spirit Reborn U-12 North Bengkulu Players
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of Small Sided Games (SSG) training assisted by the Blue Lock anime on the shooting ability of SSB Spirit Reborn players aged 10–12 years in North Bengkulu. This study used an experimental method with a One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The research sample consisted of 24 players selected using a purposive sampling technique. The treatment was carried out for six weeks with a total of 18 meetings. The research instrument used a soccer shooting ability test for 10–12 years old. The results showed an average increase from 18.33 in the pretest to 28.70 in the posttest with a percentage increase of 56.59%. The t-test produced a t-count value of -31.56 greater than the t-table of -2.06 at a significance level of 0.05, so there is a significant effect of SSG training assisted by the Blue Lock anime on shooting ability. In conclusion, Small Sided Games training assisted by the Blue Lock anime effectively increases the accuracy, strength, and motivation of players in shooting soccer

title: Character Building and Discipline in Adolescents: A Case Study at Bunga Sejati Pencak Silat School, Tantan Village, Muaro Jambi Regency
abstract: This study aims to describe and analyse the process of character building for discipline among adolescents at the Bunga Sejati Ranting Tantan Pencak Silat Academy, Tantan Village, Muaro Jambi Regency. The study uses a qualitative approach with a case study design to gain an in-depth understanding of the coaching practices that take place in real life at the pencak silat academy. The research participants consisted of six key informants, namely the Village Head, administrators, coaches, community leaders, and two active students. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participatory observation, and documentation, then analysed using NVivo software through the stages of open coding, axial coding, and thematic analysis. The results of the study identified six main themes in discipline character building, namely Regular Training, Strict Rules, Exemplary Coach, Punctuality, Responsibility, and Respectful Attitude. The findings show that regular training is the foundation for building discipline through consistent habituation, supported by the application of strict rules and the exemplary behaviour of coaches as social models. title: The Relationship between Self-Confidence and Emotion Regulation in Pencak Silat Extracurricular Students in Elementary School
abstract: This study aimed to examine the relationship between self-confidence and emotion regulation among elementary school students participating in pencak silat extracurricular activities at Integrated Islamic Elementary School Alief Mardiyah. This study employed a quantitative correlational design. The population consisted of all students participating in the extracurricular program, with a total sample of 30 students selected using a total sampling technique. Data were collected using a self-confidence questionnaire adapted from the Students' Confidence with Key Skills (SICKS) instrument and a self-regulation questionnaire adapted from the Self-Rating Scale of Self-Directed Learning (SRSSDL), focusing on indicators related to emotional management and self-control. Data analysis included descriptive statistics, normality testing, and Pearson Product Moment correlation analysis. The results showed that the mean score of self-confidence was 69.53 (SD = 9.21), indicating a moderate level of self-confidence, while the mean score of emotion regulation was 91.76 (SD = 10.34), indicating a good level of emotion regulation. title: Study of Physical Literacy Levels Based on Gender and Socioeconomic Status among Phase B Elementary School Students in Sukakarya Village
abstract: Physical literacy is an important aspect of physical education that supports the development of skills and student participation in physical activities. This study aims to analyze the level of physical literacy among Phase B elementary school students based on gender and socioeconomic status in rural areas. This study employs a quantitative approach with a descriptive-comparative design. The study subjects consisted of 180 students selected using total sampling. Data were collected using a physical literacy questionnaire and a socioeconomic status questionnaire, then analyzed descriptively and through nonparametric statistical procedures. The results indicate no significant difference in physical literacy between male and female students. Socioeconomic status was categorized from questionnaire scores, with male students consisting of 11 low, 74 medium, and 5 high SES students, while female students consisted of 9 low, 78 medium, and 3 high SES students. These findings suggest that students’ physical literacy is relatively uniform and that socioeconomic status in this sample is dominated by the medium category. title: Analysis of the Contribution of Upper Body Muscle Power to Hook Punch Power in Boxers
abstract: Among boxers at the Cyber Fight Academy, this study investigated the relationship between explosive hook punch ability and hook punch strength. A quantitative approach with a correlational design was used. Employing total sampling, this study involved twelve selected boxers. The instruments used included a punch power machine to measure hook punch strength and a 30-second explosive push-up test to measure arm muscle explosive strength. Normality tests, Pearson’s correlation, and simple linear regression were used to analyze the data. The results showed that the data were normally distributed with a significance value greater than 0.05; the linear regression test showed a significance value of 0.028 (less than 0.05), indicating a significant relationship between explosive punch ability and hook punch strength. The average hook punch power was 770, and the average explosive punch strength was 23.50. This study found that the ability to explosively activate the arm muscles through high-intensity push-ups has a significant influence on the hook punch power of boxers. title: Improving Student Creativity and Cohesiveness in Physical Education Learning through Gemu Fa Mi Re Gymnastics
abstract: This study aims to improve students' creativity and teamwork in Physical Education, Sports, and Health through Gemu Fa Mi Re Gymnastics for fifth-grade students at South Landasan Ulin Elementary School 1. This study used the Classroom Action Research (CAR) method with the Kemmis and McTaggart model, which consists of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The study was conducted in two cycles. Data collection techniques included observation, performance assessment, and documentation. Data were analyzed descriptively using qualitative and quantitative methods. The results showed that the implementation of Gemu Fa Mi Re Gymnastics can improve students' creativity and teamwork in physical education learning. This improvement was evident in student participation and enthusiasm, which increased from 70% in the pre-cycle to 95% in the second cycle. Students' basic movement skills also increased from 65% to 85%, while positive responses to learning increased from 75% to 90%. Furthermore, students became more enthusiastic, confident, able to develop a variety of movements, and worked better together in group activities. title: The Effect of Coach Communication on Football Athletes' Achievement Motivation with the Training Environment as a Mediating Variable in Southwest Papua.
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of coach communication on the achievement motivation of soccer athletes, with the training environment as a mediating variable. This type of research is explanatory research. The population in this study consisted of soccer athletes who are members of Soccer Schools (SSB) in Southwest Papua Province. The sample size, calculated using Hair's formula, consisted of 220 athletes. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling. The instrument for coach communication was the Scale for Effective Communication in Team Sports-2 (SECTS-2), and for achievement motivation, the Achievement Motivation Scale for Sports Environment (AMSSE). The data analysis technique used was PLS-SEM. The results of the study showed that coach communication has a positive effect on the achievement motivation of soccer athletes through the training environment, with a t-statistic of 1.985 and a p-value of 0.047. The findings of this study provide important contributions, both theoretically and practically, in understanding how coach communication can influence the achievement motivation of soccer athletes, with the training environment as a mediating variable. title: Passing Accuracy Among Football Players of Junior High School N40 Muara Niro in Tebo Regency
abstract: This study aims to determine the level of passing accuracy among football players of Junior High School 40 Muara Niro, Tebo Regency, and to analyze the results of passing accuracy based on technical indicators including pass direction, pass strength, and target accuracy. This research uses a quantitative approach with a descriptive research type. The population in this study consisted of 20 students, all of whom were used as the sample through a total sampling technique. Data collection techniques employed a passing skill test, while data analysis used descriptive statistics in the form of mean, percentage, and category classification. The results of the study show that the students' level of passing accuracy falls into the “good” category with an average score of 7.45. The score distribution indicates that most students are in the range of scores 7 and 8, with a dominant percentage between 70% and 80%. Classically, 75% of students are in the good category, 15% in the very good category, and 10% in the fair category. There are no students in the poor or very poor categories. title: Analysis of the Contribution of Lower Limb Muscle Power to Footwork in Boxers
abstract: This study aims to analyze the contribution of lower-body muscle power to footwork ability in boxers. A quantitative strategy with a descriptive correlational design was employed. Twelve amateur boxers from the Cyber Fight Academy in Semarang were chosen for the study using complete sampling. The Vertical Jump Test was used to measure lower-body muscle power, and a modified Cone Footwork T-test designed for boxing movement characteristics was used to analyze footwork ability. Descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, correlation, and linear regression tests were used to examine the data at a significance level of 0.05. The findings demonstrated a normal distribution of the data with a significance level greater than 0.05. title: The Effectiveness of Traditional Sports on Self-Confidence and Social Interaction in Inclusive Physical Education: A Narrative Review
abstract: Objectives: This review was conducted to examine the current literature on how adapted traditional sports can build self-confidence and enhance social interaction among students in inclusive physical education classes. Materials and Methods: This study employed a literature review method. Articles were searched for across various academic databases using specific criteria, namely studies that discuss modifications to local games and measure their impact on students’ psychosocial conditions. Data from these various journals were then synthesized using qualitative narrative analysis. Results: Various studies indicate that traditional games are highly adaptable—such as through adjustments to equipment or relaxing rules. This has proven effective in reducing competitive pressure, enabling students with special needs to feel more capable and confident. Additionally, the inherent nature of local games, which requires effective teamwork, breaks down social barriers, fosters empathy among regular students, and helps students with special needs feel accepted by their peers. title: Implementation of Modified Basketball Games in Teaching Throwing and Catching Skills
abstract: This study aims to describe students’ ball throwing and catching abilities after participating in a modified basketball game. The research method used was a quantitative approach with a one-shot pre-experimental case study design. This pre-experimental study was conducted on a single group and did not involve a control group. The sample in this study consisted of 28 sixth grade students from Class 6 C at Cindai Alus 2 Public Elementary School. The research instruments used in the posttest included throwing and catching tests, observations of throwing movements comprising preparation, execution, and follow through, as well as observations of attitudes, including cooperation, honesty, self confidence, respect, and discipline. Data analysis employed descriptive statistical techniques. The results of this study indicate that students’ throwing and catching skills, on average, fell into the “Enough” category following the implementation of the modified basketball game. Thus, these findings suggest that instruction using the modified basketball game is associated with students’ throwing and catching skills as well as their attitudes toward physical education activities.

title: The Effectiveness of Cooperative Soccer Like Games on Gross and Social Motor
abstract: This study aims to test the effectiveness of soccer like games learning with a cooperative approach in improving gross motor skills and social skills of elementary school students. The research uses the design of Classroom Action Research (PTK) which is carried out in three cycles each of which includes the stages of planning, implementation of actions, observation, and reflection, with subjects of 45 elementary school students. The instruments used are the Test of Gross Motor Development (TGMD) to measure gross motor skills and the Social Skills Rating System (SSRS) to assess social skills, both of which are standard instruments that are widely used in children's education and physical education research. The results showed an increase in gross motor score from 48.9 in cycle I to 66.6 in cycle II and 80 in cycle III, while social skills score increased from 33.3 in cycle I to 60 in cycle II and 82.2 in cycle III. These findings show that game-based learning combined with a cooperative approach is effective in developing gross motor skills as well as social skills of elementary school students simultaneously.

title: The Relationship Between Sleep Patterns and the Physical Fitness Levels of Students at Junior High School 10 Semarang as Measured by the Nusantara Student Fitness Test (TKPN)
abstract: Objective: This study examined the relationship between sleep pattern and physical fitness among junior high school students of Junior High School 10 Semarang using the Nusantara Student Fitness Test (TKPN). Materials and methods: A quantitative cross-sectional correlational design was used with total sampling of 32 students in class VIII G. Sleep data were taken from an archived 15-item questionnaire adapted from the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and provided as total scores and categories in the research dataset. Physical fitness was assessed with TKPN components, namely PACER, sit-up, squat thrust, and V sit and reach. Each TKPN component was converted into age- and sex-specific scores using the official Kemenpora norms, then combined with the weighted TKPN formula. Descriptive statistics, Shapiro-Wilk normality tests, and Spearman’s rho were applied at α = 0.05. Results: Most students showed poor sleep (78.1%). Fitness levels were predominantly poor (65.6%) and very poor (9.4%), whereas only 6.3% reached the good category. title: Examining Self-Confidence and Mental Toughness Among U-16 Athletes at Darul Amanah Football Academy
abstract: This study aims to examine aspects of sports psychology, including self-confidence and mental toughness, among 16 year-old soccer athletes at the Darul Amanah Football Academy. The method used in this study is descriptive, with a quantitative research design. The study participants consisted of the entire population of Darul Amanah Football Academy (FA) U-16 athletes, totaling 25 individuals; therefore, the sampling technique applied was total sampling. Data were collected through an online questionnaire Using the Athlete Self-Confidence Questionnaire (ASQ) as a tool to measure self-confidence levels and The Sports Mental Toughness Questionnaire (SMTQ) was utilized to assess mental toughness. The results of the descriptive statistical analysis showed that the average self-confidence score of the athletes was 38.24, with the majority falling into the moderate category (56%). Meanwhile, the average mental toughness score was 42.20, with the majority falling into the high category (56%). No athletes were found to be in the low category for either of these variables. title: The Effect of Shuttlecock LED Bowling Games on the Accuracy of Short Serves in Badminton among Junior High School Students
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of the LED Shuttlecock Bowling game on improving short serve accuracy in badminton among junior high school students. The research employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design. The sample consisted of 35 eighth-grade students from SMP Negeri 1 Soko, selected through purposive sampling. The research instrument was an assessment sheet for the short serve accuracy test. The intervention was conducted in six sessions, consisting of one pretest session, four treatment sessions using the LED Shuttlecock Bowling game, and one posttest session. Data analysis techniques included descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk normality test, and a paired-sample t-test with a significance level of α = 0.05. title: The Effect of Drill Training Using Dummy Throwing on Improving Pelting Technique Ability in Pencak Silat Athletes
abstract: This study aims to determine the effectiveness of drill training using a throwing dummy in improving falling technique ability. The purpose of this study is to determine the effect of drill training using a throwing dummy on the improvement of falling technique ability. Specifically, this study aims to analyze the differences in athletes' falling technique ability before and after being given drill training treatment using a throwing dummy. The research used is a pre-experimental design with a one-group pretest–posttest design, namely providing an initial test (pretest), training treatment, and a final test (posttest) to one sample group. The research sample consisted of six male adolescent pencak silat athletes in Class C who were selected using a purposive sampling technique. The research instrument was an observation sheet of falling techniques. Data analysis was conducted using a normality test to determine data distribution and was followed by a paired sample t-test to determine the differences between pretest and posttest results. title: The Effect of the Roblox Obby Real Life Game-Based Learning Model on Elementary School Students’ Gross Motor Skills
abstract: This study aimed to analyze the effect of implementing the Roblox Obby Real Life game-based learning model on elementary school students’ gross motor skills. The study employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design. The participants consisted of 30 students from grades IV to VI at UPT Elementary School Wangi II, selected through a total sampling technique. The research instrument was an observation sheet assessing gross motor skills across five aspects: agility, strength and explosive power, balance, accuracy, and body coordination, using a four-point rubric scale. The intervention was conducted over six sessions, consisting of one pretest session, four intervention sessions, and one posttest session. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk normality test, and a paired sample t-test with a significance level of α = 0.05. title: The Influence of Hanging Ball Media in Increasing the Accuracy of the Sickle Kicking Technique in Pencak Silat Athletes
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of using hanging ball media on the accuracy of crescent kicks in pencak silat athletes. The crescent kick is one of the techniques frequently used in pencak silat competitions and plays an important role in scoring points, so kick accuracy becomes an important factor in athletes’ performance. The material used in this study was hanging ball media which functioned as a training target to improve kick accuracy. The research method used was a pre-experimental method with a one group pretest–posttest design. The sample consisted of 20 pencak silat athletes selected using a purposive sampling technique, namely athletes who actively participated in training and had mastered the basic crescent kick technique. The research instrument used was a crescent kick accuracy test. Data were collected through a pretest before treatment and a posttest after training using hanging ball media. title: Effects of Beetroot Juice Supplementation on Metabolic Response and Physical Performance in Athletes
abstract: This study examined the effect of dietary nitrate-rich beetroot juice on metabolic responses and physical performance in active athletes. Using a randomized controlled design, 30 athletes from different sport backgrounds were assigned to an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group consumed a standardized dose of beetroot juice before exercise, while the control group received no supplementation. Metabolic responses were assessed through blood glucose, insulin, and lactate concentration, while performance was measured using the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test. The results showed significant differences between groups (p ≤ 0.05). Athletes who consumed beetroot juice had lower lactate concentrations, suggesting better metabolic efficiency and delayed fatigue during exercise. They also covered a greater distance in the endurance test compared with the control group. In addition, improved insulin response indicated more efficient energy use during physical activity. These findings suggest that beetroot juice may support athletic performance by improving metabolic function, reducing fatigue-related by-products, and enhancing endurance capacity. title: Physical Fitness Training Strategies to Improve Operational Readiness of Indonesian Army Soldiers in High-Risk Areas of Papua
abstract: Physical fitness training plays a strategic role in preparing Indonesian Army (TNI AD) soldiers for Security Operations in Conflict-Prone Areas (Pamrahwan) in Papua, which are characterized by rugged terrain, extreme weather, and dynamic threat conditions. This study aims to analyze the physical fitness condition of Pamrahwan soldiers, identify constraints in physical fitness training within operational areas, and formulate effective training strategies to enhance operational readiness. A qualitative approach was employed through in-depth interviews with soldiers, physical fitness instructors (Bajas/Pajas), and command elements. Data were analyzed using NVivo through coding, categorization, and thematic analysis. The findings indicate that soldiers’ physical fitness levels are generally functional and adaptive; however, training has not been fully implemented through structured, periodization-based programs. Key constraints include environmental conditions, limited facilities, security threats, and intensive operational schedules. title: Analyzing the Impact of the Nike Run Club Application on the Running Performance of Yonif 731/Kabaresi Soldiers in Maluku
abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of using the Nike Run Club (NRC) application on the running performance improvement of Yonif 731/Kabaresi soldiers in Maluku. The background of this research arises from the need for an effective and measurable military physical training program, as running is one of the vital components in the Indonesian Army’s physical fitness assessment. The research employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design. The population consisted of 731 soldiers, while the sample size was determined using the Slovin formula, resulting in 88 respondents selected through simple random sampling. The research instrument comprised a questionnaire covering three main dimensions, namely perception of NRC, training motivation and consistency, and benefits for running ability, measured using a 5-point Likert scale. In addition, an objective measurement was conducted through a 3,200-meter running test before and after using NRC. Data analysis included validity and reliability tests, descriptive statistics, and hypothesis testing using a one-sample t-test and paired pre–post comparison. title: Improving Fine Motor Skills Through Tapping Activities In Group B Children At Beringin Indah Early Childhood Education Center South Bengkulu
abstract: The purpose of this study is to improve the motor skills of children in group B of Early Childhood Education (PAUD) by using banana stems as a medium. Through two cycles starting from planning, implementation, observation, and reflection is the method used to conduct this study. Ten children with a total of seven boys and three girls are the subjects of the study. Classroom Action Research (CAR) is the type of research used in this study. The methods used to collect data are observation, interviews, and documentation. The instruments used are assessment sheets and observation instruments. This study uses quantitative data analysis techniques using statistical analysis. The results showed that children's fine motor skills in the pre-cycle were 42.50%, in cycle 1 it was obtained 70.83% and cycle II reached 83.33%. This concludes that stamping activities using banana stems can improve fine motor skills in children in group B of PAUD Beringin Indah well and optimally.

title: The Correlation Between Leg Muscle Strength, Balance, and Reaction Speed to the Ability of the Crescent Kick
abstract: This study aims to determine the correlation between leg muscle strength, balance, and reaction speed to the ability of the sickle kick in pencak silat athletes Elementary School 1 Bangilan. The study used a correlational method with a quantitative approach. The population and sample in this study were all 20 students of the pencak silat extracurricular Elementary School 1 Bangilan with a saturated sampling technique. The research instruments included a leg muscle strength test using a vertical jump, a balance test using a standing stork test, a reaction speed test using a 10-meter run, and a 10-second sickle kick ability test. Data analysis was carried out using the Pearson Product Moment correlation test and multiple linear regression with the help of the SPSS 23 program. title: Development of a Dribbling Technique Skills Training Model in Futsal Games for PJKR Students of the 2024 Class at Tadulako University
abstract: This study aims to develop a dribbling technique skill training model in futsal games for PJKR students of the 2024 class of Tadulako University. The method used is research and development (R&D) with the Borg and Gall model. The research subjects consisted of 10 students in the small group trial and 30 students in the large group trial. Data collection was carried out through a validation questionnaire from futsal experts, learning experts, and student response questionnaires, then analyzed using descriptive percentage techniques. The validation results showed that the assessment of futsal experts 1 and 2 was 63%, respectively, and the learning expert was 84%, with the category used. The results of the small group trial obtained a percentage of 80% and the large group 79%, both of which were in the category used. Based on these results, it can be concluded that the developed dribbling technique training model is feasible to use and can improve basic dribbling technique skills and student interest in futsal learning.

title: Forearm Passing Proficienci : A Skills Movement Analysis of Student Athletes In Volleyball
abstract: Volleyball is a sport that requires technical skills, coordination, and good motor abilities. Mastery of basic techniques is a crucial factor in supporting overall playing performance, particularly the forearm pass, which serves as the initial step in building an attack as well as maintaining ball control against the opponent’s offense. This study aims to analyze the forearm passing movement skills of student-athletes based on the preparation, execution, and follow-through phases. This research employed a quantitative descriptive design, with Kinovea version 0.9.5 as the primary instrument for motion analysis. A total of 10 students were selected as research subjects through basic technique observation and joint angle measurement. The results show that 2 students (20%) fell into the “very accurate” category, 7 students (70%) into the “accurate” category, and 1 student (10%) into the “less accurate” category. Kinematic analysis recorded an average knee flexion angle of 106.96° (range 83°–132.9°) and an average shoulder extension angle of 97.05° (range 80.5°–123.2°), both of which fall within the effective range for supporting body stability and ball control. title: The Influence of AI-Driven Learning Media on Football Motivation and Passing Ability
abstract: This study aims to test the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI)-based learning media in improving students' soccer passing skills and learning motivation compared to conventional learning. The study used a quasi-experimental design with a pretest–posttest control group pattern on 60 FIK UNIMED students who were divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group received AI-based learning with real-time feedback, personalized training, and gamification elements, while the control group used conventional methods. The research instruments included a passing skills test and a learning motivation scale. Data analysis used ANCOVA/t-test and Pearson correlation. title: Level of Public Satisfaction with Sports Facilities at Medan State University Stadium
abstract: This study aims to determine the level of public satisfaction with the sports facilities at the Medan State University Stadium. The study used a quantitative descriptive approach involving 30 respondents, consisting of students and the general public who use the stadium facilities. The research instrument was a closed-ended questionnaire using a Likert scale covering indicators of facility and infrastructure conditions, cleanliness, security, comfort, accessibility, and facility management. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS)to obtain percentage values, average (mean), and satisfaction level categories. The results of the analysis show that the level of public satisfaction is in the category Good with an overall average score of 3.87 (scale 1–5) or 77.4%. The aspects of cleanliness (mean = 4.02) and security (mean = 3.95) obtained the highest scores, while the aspect of completeness and maintenance of facilities (mean = 3.65) obtained the lowest score.
